claim:
Let \(\psi:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) be
\[
\psi(t)=
\begin{cases}
1-t,&0\le t\le\frac18,\\
\frac{11-4t}{12},&\frac18\le t\le\frac12,\\
\frac{1+t}{2},&\frac12\le t\le1,
\end{cases}
\]
and let \(X=\ell_\psi-\ell_\infty\) be the real generalized Day--James plane whose norm is the absolute normalized \(\psi\)-norm when the coordinate product is nonnegative and the \(\ell_\infty\)-norm when it is nonpositive. Then
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)=\frac{13}{9}.
\]
The value is attained by
\[
x=\left(-\frac23,-\frac23\right),\qquad
y=\left(\frac32,-\frac32\right),\qquad
z=\left(\frac56,-\frac{13}{6}\right).
\]

correctness.rationale: The source definition reconstructs the eight unit-ball edges. For q(a,b)=a^2+(10/13)ab+b^2, exact edgewise minimization gives m=144/169 and exact vertex evaluation gives M=16/13. The Hilbert sandwich implies C_Pt<=M/m=13/9. The explicit triple has exact norm data 1,3/2,13/6,13/6,3/2,1 and ratio 13/9.
risks: All polygon edges are treated exactly; no numerical sampling is used for the continuous claim.

Exact Ptolemy theory in the closest literature is built for the absolute class, so determining the four-point constant of this standard nonabsolute example tests a natural boundary of that theory. The global Hilbert sandwich and explicit saturating triple make the result structural rather than an arbitrary polygon computation.
